newsitem.title: USA: CME live cattle seen lower, feeders steady to off.
newsitem.headline: CME live cattle seen lower, feeders steady to off.

text.p: CME live cattle futures were expected to open 0.100 to 1.000 cent per lb lower while feeder cattle were called steady to 0.100 lower, livestock analysts said.
A bearishly-construed monthly USDA Cattle-on-Feed report and growing concern over E.coli in hamburger meat should weigh on live cattle futures at the start.

The USDA report showed July placements at 118 percent of last year and August 1 on-feed supplies at 119 percent, both well above the high end of expectations. Most of the pressure in futures is seen in the December contract from this report, they said.

The USDA also announced Friday the largest recall of U.S. ground beef products in history due to potential contamination by E.coli bacteria. Hudson Foods Inc is recalling 1.2 million lbs of frozen beef patties which may prompt nervous liquidation in live cattle futures, they said.
Despite lower corn futures indications, feeder cattle futures are seen trading steady to lower on expected spillover pressure from live cattle futures, they added.
The latest CME feeder cattle index dipped $0.03 to $80.87 per cwt.
